findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed employees donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was abolished. Ensure that staff remember to wash their hands before donning gloves at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-101.11: At the start of the inspection, there was no designated PIC and no one in the facility was present in the facility with an active CFM. When the permit holder is the PIC and is not present in the facility, a designated PIC must be present in the facility with an active CFM. The permit holder/PIC was present by the end of the inspection with an active CFM. Ensure a designated PIC with an active CFM is available during all hours of operation. findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:

Ensure that test strips are used at regular intervals and that sanitizer buckets are changed out at a frequency necessary to maintain the sanitizer’s efficacy. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: There are several items in the walk-in cooler observed without a date mark on the container. Ensure all items in the walk-in cooler are dated with either the date of their prep or the date they need to be discarded. This item will be observed during the 01/19/2024 follow-up if it has not been corrected by the 01/16/2024 follow-up.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

4-101.11: The service counter is observed to be repaired with duct tape that has started to detach from the surface. This surface needs to be repaired properly to not allow the migration of deleterious substances.
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: There is observed a board being used as a support for the service table near the cold and hot holding. This board is observed with tape, a screw sticking out, and porous. This board to be used in this manner needs to have the tape removed, remove and items causing projections (such as the screw), and needs to be painted or sealed to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface. While reviewing the report, the board was removed from service and replaced with a metal pipe. This pipe is approved for use in this manner as it is smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The following areas are observed to have an accumulation of food debris/soil and needs to be cleaned and sanitized:
-The ice cream machine that is not in use at this moment needs to have its surfaces cleaned.
-The vegetable cold holding cooler has visible soil and food debris on multiple of its surfaces internally that need to be cleaned.
-The double door freezer has food debris on the bottom that will need to be cleaned out.
Ensure these areas receive attention to detail when cleaning and are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
(B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12:  The following locations in the facility are observed to be soiled with food debris/soils and need to be cleaned and sanitized:
-The wall behind the prep coolers is observed to have an excessive amount of food splash and will need cleaned.
-The floor behind the margarita machines in the lobby needs to be cleaned. Pull the table away from the wall to complete this task.
Ensure these areas are cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: During the inspection, multiple employees were observed switching between tasks without washing their hands. Staff should be educated and lessons performed on when and how to properly wash hands. PIC was informed and corrections on this behavior have taken place during today’s inspection.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The can opener blade was observed to have an accumulation of food debris/soil. This items was removed from service and placed into the dish area for a wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. Ensure this items is cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of food debris/soil residue.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: When tested, there was no sanitizer available in the sanitizer solution. During the inspection a correct sanitizer bucket was created and tested at appropriate levels of bleach at 100ppm. Ensure test strips are utilized every time a sanitizer bucket is created to ensure the sanitizer solution is adequate enough for the sanitizer to function properly.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: Soda nozzles in the kitchen were observed to have an accumulation of mold/soil reside inside the dispenser nozzles. Ensure this surface is washed, rinsed and sanitized at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of soil/mold residues.
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.12: The microwave in the kitchen is observed to have an accumulation of food/soil residues. Ensure the internal surfaces and the seals are cleaned and sanitized and then cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of soil/residues. 
4-602.12: (A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: A fly strip is observed to be hanging in the open space where the dish area is located. This area is located near a food prep station. The fly strip needs to be moved closer to the edge of the sink and dish machine or closer to the door in order to ensure the food items in the facility are protected from potential contaminants from the fly strip. 
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306.

findings.comment:
4-602.13: The air vents in the kitchen and the dehumidifier in the walk-in cooler are observed to have an accumulation of dust/soil residues. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned and sanitized and then cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of soil residues.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: The mop in the dry storage area was observed to be stored in the basin of the mop bucket and unable to air dry. The mop was removed from the basin and placed into the top portion of the mop bucket to allow for adequate air drying to take place. Ensure this practice continues.
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.comment:
6-501.12: It is observed that along walls and crevices along the floor that food debris and soil is present. Ensure that deep cleaning and detailed cleaning takes place at a frequency necessary to maintain the physical facility.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

If the equipment is no longer in use, it should be removed form the facility to allow for adequate cleaning to take place and to prevent areas of debris accumulation.
6-501.114: The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The caulking of the triple sink is observed to have an excessive amount of mold/soil residue. Ensure this surface receives more detailed cleaning and if the caulking is unable to be cleaned, remove the current soiled seal and replace it with a fresh seal of caulking. Continuously clean this surface at a freqeuncy necessary to prevent this accumulation of mold/soil residue.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The air vents int he kitchen are observed to have an accumulation of dust/debris. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of dust/debris which will help to prevent the potential contamination of food and food surfaces in the kitchen areas.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.comment:
4-602.11: The can opener was observed to have an accumulation of food debris and other soil. This item was removed from service and placed into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle during the inspection. Ensure this item is washed, rinsed, and sanitized after contamination.
4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: Facility was observed to have an excessive amount of drain flies in the back storage room where the mop sink is located. Inspector recommended to the facility to contact their pest control operator (Bacon’s) and obtain an enzymatic cleaner for the use of eradicating the drain fly infestation. A follow-up will occur on November 19th, 2021 to investigate the issue and determine it resolved or not. Ensure cleaning and sanitizing takes place in the areas where drain flies are present.
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: The dry spices and tortilla shells were observed to be uncovered on the lower shelving in the dry storage areas. Ensure that these containers are covered to prevent contamination from the shelving items above.
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: Wiping cloths were observed to be stored on the counter and not in a sanitizer solution. These cloths were placed into a sanitizer solution to be held between tasks. Ensure this practice continues in order to prevent contamination form the cloths after being used.
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: The scoop used for the dry rice was observed to be stored within the rice itself and not above the food’s surface. Ensure that the scoops are stored in a manner that does not potentially create a source of contamination.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: No sanitizer solution was available during the start of the inspection. After inspector spoke with cook, a sanitizer solution was created and measured at 200ppm Bleach. Ensure that a sanitizer solution is available during all hours of operation.
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: The mop was observed to be stored in the mop basin and not in a position to air dry. Ensure the mop is placed in a position that allows it to air dry such as hanging on the wall or in the top portion of the mop bucket.
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The caulking along the triple sink is in need of replacement and the prep sink is in need of caulking. Strip the old caulking and replace it with a fresh seal that is smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
